findings.summary: isPublished(article) dereferences article.draft with no guard for article being undefined. articles.get(match[1]) (line 44) returns undefined for any /blog/<slug> link whose slug isn't in the articles map — a typo'd slug, a renamed/deleted post, or a real site route like /blog/2 (the pagination page the site's own [...page].astro generates via paginate()). Reproduced directly: running the plugin's transform on a tree containing a link to /blog/2 throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading draft)', a synchronous throw inside a remark transform that fails the entire Astro build, not just that one file. This inverts the brief's intent — 'no dead or premature link ships' was meant to make bad links non-fatal, but an unresolvable slug is now a harder failure than the dead link it replaces (previously such a link just rendered as a normal, possibly-404ing anchor; now it takes the whole build down). Needs a guard, e.g. `if (!article || article.draft) return false;`.
